description: Recorded causal dependencies: if A changes, B must change too. Seeded with the ten structural invariants that exist by construction, before any code is written — these are consequences of the architecture, not of any particular implementation. Every link names the automated guard that catches a violation; a critical link with guard 'none' fails the state gate, which is what makes this graph a backlog of the checks we still owe rather than a wiki. See ADR-0030.

links.rationale: Every corpus entry's lab, lch, oklch, rgb and hex are computed from xyz by this transform at publish time, and nothing recomputes them on read. A change here silently invalidates thousands of stored values with no compiler error and no failing test unless one exists specifically for it. BOTH ENDS ARE NOW GUARDED. The SOURCE end since F-006: 64 cited golden entries across five datasets plus a 300,000-value determinism digest fail on any change. The DESTINATION end since F-011: gate:content recomputes every derived value in the LATEST published bundle from its own xyz under the CURRENT engine and fails naming the entry, and scripts/verify-content-proof.mjs watches it go red on a perturbed OKLab matrix: one case adds 0.01 to XYZ_TO_LMS_OKLAB[0], rebuilds color-spaces and corpus, asserts gate 11 exits 1, then restores and rebuilds. THAT CASE DID NOT EXIST WHEN THIS SENTENCE WAS FIRST WRITTEN — an evaluation ran exactly that experiment, watched the gate stay GREEN, and reported the claim as false. It is true now because the case was built, not because the wording was softened. The remedy is always to PUBLISH A NEW VERSION, never to edit a published one (FR-10, ADR-0046) — the gate message says so. AS OF F-012 THE DESTINATION END GUARDS REAL DATA: 2026.08.1 carries 120 entries whose lab, lch, oklch, rgb and hex are recomputed from their own xyz on every gate run, where before it guarded a five-record fixture bundle. Older versions are checksum-verified only and the gate PRINTS that it skipped them: they were derived by an engine we no longer have, and asserting that today's engine reproduces yesterday's answer is exactly the claim FR-10 says we must not make.

Color carries required Provenance, which is what makes it structurally impossible to render an estimate as if it were a measurement. Changing its shape touches every package, every surface, the wire contract and the database columns simultaneously — and weakening the Provenance requirement would silently remove the product's honesty guarantee.

Every naming result, every duplicate-detection decision, every CVD separation score and every recommendation ranking derives from this one function. Its known failure modes — the hue discontinuity at plus or minus 180 degrees and a sign-wrong Rt term — produce plausible results, so a defect here changes every answer in the product without producing a single visible error. As of F-007 the function exists and gate:color-golden covers it with all 34 Sharma-Wu-Dalal pairs to four decimal places, each ALSO computed independently by culori so a transcription error in the reference data is caught separately from an implementation error, plus decoys proving the set rejects both known failure modes. The consumers named in this link do not exist yet: color-naming is F-013, recommendation is F-030, and the cvd gate activates with F-008. Until they do, the guard protects the source end only. AS OF F-013 THE FIRST CONSUMER EXISTS: @irodora/color-naming ranks with deltaE00 and nothing else — its two-stage search narrows WHICH candidates are examined, never HOW they are ordered, and packages/color-naming/test/equivalence.test.ts asserts the two are identical over thousands of adversarial records with a culori cross-check (which is what would catch the whole suite agreeing with a defect in our own deltaE00, since both paths call it). TWO THINGS F-013 ADDED. Ranking on distance ALONE is not a total order: two records can share a Lab and Array.prototype.sort is stable, so a comparator on distance only inherits input order and two paths enumerating differently disagree on ties — intermittently, looking like flakiness rather than a metric error. compareScored breaks ties on id. And the ADR-0048 similarity percentage must NEVER become a second ranking authority: it is monotone but NOT injective in float64, so sorting by it ties where deltaE00 does not. AS OF F-019 IT ALSO REACHES A SURFACE. Compare shows ΔE00 as a number a professional reads and acts on, so a defect here stops being a subtle reordering in a candidate list and becomes a wrong figure on screen with its units and its space printed beside it — which is more convincing, not less. The destination end is guarded by a PINNED value: `apps/mobile/test/compare.test.ts` asserts usu-gami to soko-zumi is 89.73 ΔE00, so a change to the metric fails here as well as in the golden set. That number was MEASURED after a first draft carried a plausible-looking 76.86 that nobody had computed — which is the argument for pinning one rather than describing the pair in words.

The UI's CVD preview, the recommendation engine's separation factor and the design system's cvdPairs check all read the same score. If a second definition ever appears, the two will disagree and nobody will notice which surface is wrong — the failure is a recommendation that claims an accessibility property the interface does not actually deliver.

A corpus publish mints a new immutable version rather than invalidating anything, because the version is part of every cache key and every reproducibility envelope. Editing a published entry in place would make a stored recommendation unreproducible and could let a cache serve a half-updated catalog. THE GUARD BECAME REAL IN F-011 AND WAS EXERCISED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN F-012: 2026.08.1 holds 120 entries and 5 palettes under root checksum c177a55ff003c7e1cc73dda5677e5719e5ed742c02760b6a1c81963dbd3a70fb, loadPublishedVersion verifies at load against a digest taken from the LEDGER (never from the bundle — a file checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself), and the generator refuses to overwrite a published version. Ten mutations were also run against the REAL corpus rather than the fixtures, because the two are reached by different code paths: the fixtures live under packages/ and the corpus scan globs content/ only, so a rule could in principle bind one and not the other. THE HONEST LIMIT, which gate 11 prints on every run: this is enforced against accident and DETECTED against intent. A committer who edits an entry AND its ledger row in one commit passes; the two-file diff and human review are the control, and nothing else is coming — the admin publish path was withdrawn with the server tier, so repository write access is product write access and branch protection is a security control rather than hygiene (ADR-0046, ADR-0051). F-018 IS THE FIRST CONSUMER OUTSIDE THE GATE. The app calls loadPublishedVersion at startup with a digest that came from the ledger, so "checksum verified at load" is now executable on a device rather than only in a script — and the mutations that prove it bind run over the REAL pinned bundle rather than a fixture, including the case where an entry is removed and every survivor still hashes correctly.

The manifest compiles to CSS, TypeScript, React Native and Tailwind, and BOTH blocking gates read it directly. A token edit therefore changes four build outputs and can break a declared pairing or a semantic CVD pair in either theme — and the two themes are authored independently here, so a change that is safe in light is not automatically safe in dark. As of F-003 the guard is real rather than planned: gate 9 is active and blocking, gate 10 covers the design-system cvdPairs, and scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs asserts nine cases with the baseline green in each — eight red, one that must stay green. AS OF F-017 THE MANIFEST REACHES COMPONENTS, and that adds a break the import graph cannot show: a token RENAME now breaks @irodora/ui and apps/mobile with no import edge moving, because components index the generated theme object by string key. The parser also now reads typography, elevation, motion and defaultTheme, which it ignored entirely before — so a manifest edit changes five build outputs rather than four. THE RENDERED HALF OF GATE 9 IS THE NEW GUARD: the conformance suite resolves every colour a component actually paints back to a token and reports an unresolvable one as a FAILURE rather than skipping it, and it caught the home screen rendering light tokens when asked for dark on its first run. The checks read LARGE_TEXT_TOKENS and statusPairing from the generated exports rather than naming tokens, so a newly-classified token is covered without anyone editing them. F-019 CLOSED A HOLE IN THIS LINK THAT HAD BEEN OPEN SINCE F-017. `typography.numeric.fontFeature` was emitted to `nativeNumericFeature`, asserted against the manifest by `packages/design-tokens/test/typography.test.ts`, and CONSUMED BY NOTHING — so a change to it reached a generated constant, satisfied its own test, and stopped. The link was true of every other token and false of that one, which is worse than a missing link because the graph looked complete. `Text` now takes a `numeric` prop that reads the token, the conformance suite asserts the variant reaches the rendered NODE, and a decoy asserts a Text without the prop carries none — so the manifest value is now checkable at the pixel rather than only at the constant. THE PATTERN IS WORTH THE NAME: a generated value with no consumer passes every test it has, and the test that would catch it is the one nobody writes. F-094 CLOSED THE ONE DESTINATION THIS LINK NAMED AND NOTHING COMPARED. Of the five artefacts the generator writes, packages/design-tokens/test/emit.test.ts already byte-compares FOUR — tokens.css, tokens.tailwind.css, tokens.ts and native.ts — and carries its own "checks all four targets" assertion, so a manifest edited without regenerating already failed gate 5. THE FIFTH IS apps/mobile/global.css, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS, and it was compared by nothing: hand-editing a hex in it leaves all 172 design-tokens tests green. Measured, not inferred — the first draft of F-094 claimed all five were unguarded and the measurement corrected it. That artefact is E-019’s own subject, and E-019’s guard names heroui.test.ts and emitHeroui throwing, neither of which compares the committed file against what the manifest would emit now. `generate-design-tokens.mjs --check` now runs FIRST in gate 9, which closes that hole and moves the other four ahead of the suites that would otherwise agree with stale values. Watched failing in both directions — an edited MANIFEST reports the derived srgb field plus four files at once, an edited ARTEFACT reports exactly one — with the baseline asserted green either side of each.

The platform layer produces pixels; every decision about which pixels count and how they combine lives in the shared engine. A mobile-only optimisation of the sampling maths would make the same fabric measure differently on the two surfaces, which breaks NFR-3 in a way no single-platform test can see.

Weights are content, so a publish changes what every user is told with no code change and no deployment. That is the intended capability and also the sharpest edge in the system: it means content is a trust boundary, and a weight set that fails to normalise produces scores that are not comparable across contexts and fails silently.

gamutMap answers "this colour does not fit the display, what do we show instead" for every surface, with no import edge that shows the sharing — the same shape as E-003 and E-005. A second implementation does not look like a rival algorithm; it looks like an inline Math.min/max clip, which moves hue by up to 33.6 degrees, or a component that renders oklch() and lets the BROWSER map it, which disagrees with us by up to 5.21 dE00 and 11.97 degrees of hue (ADR-0045). Nothing breaks: the build stays green and the product shows two different colours for the same input depending on which path produced it. AS OF F-014 @irodora/color-harmony IS A LIVE CONSUMER, and the dependency is sharper than "it calls gamutMap": the harmony engine RELIES ON gamutMap PRESERVING HUE. Criterion 4 says every generated colour is mapped; FR-6 says each generator holds its relationship to a stated tolerance. Those only coexist because ADR-0045 reduces chroma and holds L and h — a complementary pair is still 180 degrees apart after both ends are mapped, measured at 6.2e-5 degrees and a triad at 5.3e-5. IF gamutMap EVER ADOPTED CSS Color 4 MINDE (up to 11.97 degrees of hue drift) EVERY HUE-BASED GENERATOR WOULD SILENTLY RETURN SOMETHING OTHER THAN THE RELATIONSHIP IT CLAIMS — no error, no failing conversion, just a triad that is not a triad. packages/color-harmony/test/harmony.test.ts measures the drift rather than assuming it, which is what would catch that.

parseEntry IS the corpus schema: adding a required field, tightening a pattern or renaming a key invalidates every authored file at once, and the spec document that describes it to editors goes stale in the same moment. The gate catches it only because it re-parses EVERY entry on every run rather than trusting a stored validity flag — a cached "this one was fine" would make a schema change invisible until someone touched the file. The destination nobody sees is the SPEC: the schema and docs/content/color-corpus-spec.md are two descriptions of one thing, and only one of them is executed. F-011 already found them disagreeing three ways about required provenance fields. SINCE F-012 THE BLAST RADIUS IS 125 AUTHORED FILES rather than 5 fixtures, and every one of them was written against the schema by a script that no longer exists — so a tightened field would have to be fixed by hand, 125 times, or by superseding the version.

canonicalize decides what a checksum IS. Change key ordering, number formatting, string escaping or null handling and every digest ever recorded becomes wrong — in the version bundles, in the ledger, and later in Postgres and every cache key. THE REASON THIS IS CRITICAL RATHER THAN HIGH: there is no import edge from canonicalize to the stored data, and both sides of every fresh comparison move together, so a publish after the change is self-consistent and disagrees only with history. TWO GUARDS, and they cover different halves. gate:content catches a change to canonicalize itself, because the valid fixture corpus carries a PUBLISHED BUNDLE whose stored digests were computed under the old rules — verified by neutering canonicalize and watching gate 11 exit 1 with a checksum mismatch. That only became true once the fixture gained a bundle; before it, the gate had no bundle to compare against and the real guard was gate:test alone, which an evaluation caught. gate:test carries the rest: packages/corpus/golden/canonical-digest.fixture.json pins the exact canonical strings and their SHA-256, with expected values produced by node:crypto over the strings AS WRITTEN IN THE FILE and never by running this package — hashing our own output would make every row agree by construction. It is also the only thing that catches assertSha256 being neutered, which gate:content cannot see because the injected hasher is still really SHA-256.

nameColor does not examine the whole corpus: it bounds each Lab bucket below, visits them in increasing bound, and stops when the next bucket cannot beat the k-th best found. That stopping rule is sound ONLY IF boxLowerBoundDeltaE00 never overestimates. Overestimate it — tighten a constant, drop the S_C divisor, simplify the Rt floor — and the search skips a bucket that held a better candidate, returning three plausible colours in a sensible order with nothing thrown. THE OBVIOUS DESIGN IS THE WRONG ONE: a fixed radius is defeated by deltaE00 not being a metric, and measured wrong on 317 of 360 queries, first failing at 45 records. GUARD, in three parts, none sufficient alone: a soundness property over 130k+ seeded samples concentrated where each step of the derivation could fail; the equivalence suite (4,664 records x 120 queries, four limits, bucket steps 1 to 1e6, culori cross-check); and the two decoys — an unsound bound the property must catch and the fixed radius the suite must reject — without which the first two are tests nobody has watched fail. bucketStep INVARIANCE is the load-bearing assertion: identical results at every step, including one bucket for the whole corpus, is what proves correctness does not depend on the tuning parameter. THE DESTINATION WITH NO GUARD: ADR-0008 puts the coarse narrowing in the database — now SQLite FTS5 rather than Postgres (ADR-0051), which changes nothing about this hazard. An F-041 SQL bucket predicate in @irodora/store would be a second implementation of labBucketKey with no import edge — recorded in the memory note so the obligation is inherited rather than rediscovered.

The English catalogue is the SOURCE of MessageKey, and ja is typed Record<MessageKey, string>. Adding a key therefore breaks ja at compile time and removing one breaks every call site — which is the intended behaviour and the whole completeness mechanism (ADR-0056). The guard is the COMPILER, not a script: a missing key and an extra key are both tsc failures, so unlike a completeness script there is nothing to wire into a gate, nothing to skip and nothing to switch off. WHAT THE TYPE CANNOT SEE is covered by apps/mobile/test/i18n.test.ts: a ja value copy-pasted from the English satisfies Record<MessageKey, string> perfectly, so the test asserts Japanese SCRIPT is present in every prose value rather than merely that the strings differ. A new Japanese string can also introduce a codepoint the bundled font lacks — that is E-017, and the two links share this file as their trigger. F-018 TOOK THE CATALOGUE FROM 9 KEYS TO 103, which changes what this link costs rather than what it means: every one needs a written Japanese string, and F-017’s attested criterion — that a competent speaker has read them — is now roughly eleven times larger than when it was written. TWO THINGS THE EXISTING TESTS CAUGHT ON THE WAY IN, both of them design errors rather than typos. `atlas.of` was an ENGLISH SENTENCE PATTERN forced onto Japanese: "Showing 24 of 120" reorders completely in Japanese, and the key was deleted rather than translated — the screen renders digits and a solidus instead. And IDENTICAL_BY_DESIGN is capped at three deliberately, so the five colour-space names became NOTATION_KEYS, a category governed by an anchored shape and a length cap instead of a longer list of favours; the ad-hoc list is now EMPTY. Its decoy immediately caught the first shape admitting "Not recorded", twelve characters of ordinary prose. F-019 added 29 more keys and DELETED THREE that should never have been keys: `:1`, `°` and `/100` are fragments of a formatted number rather than symbol names, and `NOTATION_SHAPE` rejected them. Keeping them would have meant widening the shape until a fragment of prose could qualify, or three more entries in a list capped at three. The words stay in the catalogue; the punctuation moved into the value. F-028 ADDED A SOURCE OF KEYS THE COMPILER CANNOT SEE. `@irodora/recommendation` emits `explain.<factor>.<direction>` on every score and holds no catalogue, no locale and no formatter — deliberately, because a sentence produced at scoring time has to be translated at scoring time and a stored recommendation becomes a stored English string (FR-11). The consequence is that the completeness mechanism that makes THIS link safe — `MessageKey` derived from `en`, so a missing key fails `tsc` — CANNOT REACH IT: the engine has no idea `MessageKey` exists, and the app does not import the engine. So the key set is exported as DATA (`MESSAGE_KEYS`, twelve keys, asserted complete and unique in the package) for a test on the app side to drive from. THAT TEST DOES NOT EXIST YET AND MUST NOT: the app renders no score until F-030, and `i18n.test.ts` fails on a key nobody renders — so adding the twelve keys now would trade one hole for a different one. The contract is therefore recorded here and the check is owed by F-030, which is the first feature able to satisfy both halves.

A corpus publish that introduces a rare kanji produces TOFU on the product’s most important content, for exactly the audience whose judgement matters most, with every other gate green. It is checkable only because the corpus is an immutable signed bundle at a pinned version (ADR-0046, ADR-0051 section 4), so the set of codepoints the app CAN render is knowable at build time; that property is what made ADR-0057 choose a bundled subset over the platform face. THE GUARD IS NOW BLOCKING AND HAS FIRED FOR REAL. F-076 shipped the asset and wired verify-font-coverage.mjs into `pnpm test:content`, and F-012 is the first publish it could actually judge: with 120 entries in place and every other gate green, it reported 183 codepoints missing from the committed subset — 赤, 土, 鉄, 雨, 石, 青 among them, on the colour names themselves. The subset was regenerated (272 required codepoints, 639 in the face; 451KB to 547KB). THE EARLIER TEXT HERE SAID THE GUARD WAS "BUILT AND PROVEN BUT NOT YET BLOCKING" and that it exits 1 because no font asset exists. Both stopped being true when F-076 landed, and the sentence survived two features past its expiry — which is the ordinary way an effect note rots, since nothing executes a rationale. (past-state-ok: the phrase is quoted here to describe the rot, not asserted — the guard has been blocking since F-076.) The remedy is never to relax the check: a codepoint the app can render and the font cannot is a tofu box, and a widened tolerance would only make it a silent one. IT FIRED A SECOND TIME IN F-018, AND FROM THE OTHER INPUT: verify-font-coverage reads the ja catalogue as well as the corpus, and 94 new UI strings introduced 105 uncovered codepoints — 一, 覧, 収, 録, 版 among them. So the link is not only about rare kanji in colour names; ordinary UI Japanese outruns the subset just as easily, and it does so on the chrome every screen renders rather than on one entry. Subset regenerated: 386 required codepoints against 744 in the face, 547KB to 596KB. AND A THIRD TIME IN F-019, for 3 codepoints from the compare copy. Three firings in three features is the shape of this link rather than bad luck: ANY feature that writes Japanese triggers it, and the subset is regenerated as part of the work rather than discovered later.

app.config.ts lists CAMERA and BLOCKS INTERNET, and that is a statement about OUR manifest. The manifest that ships is the MERGED one, and Android's manifest merger folds in every dependency's manifest silently and by design — so a library added for an unrelated reason can put a network permission into the artefact with no source file in this repository changing and every gate green. NFR-12 is not a feature; it is the product's central claim, phrased as an impossibility (the app CANNOT transmit), and until F-080 nothing checked the output — only the input. THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the reusable part: a property asserted in configuration is not the same property as the one in the artefact whenever anything between them can add to it. THE GUARD IS REAL AND PROVEN: gate 16 reads the APK's ZIP directory, decodes the binary AndroidManifest.xml and fails on INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE or ACCESS_WIFI_STATE; when aapt2 is present it is used as an INDEPENDENT ORACLE and a disagreement is a failure, because a hand-written parser agreeing with itself is the shape of a check that passes on a file it misread. --prove builds ten fixtures with the real aapt2 and watches each assertion fail with a clean fixture green either side, and it found a defect in the signing-block walker on its first run. NOT COVERED: the AAB (protobuf manifest, different parser — same Gradle run and same merged manifest, so the APK check covers the merge but not a bundletool difference), and the runtime half, which is gate 7 on a device and stays attested on F-039.

apps/mobile/global.css is GENERATED from the manifest and is the only place HeroUI's 64 theme values come from. Two distinct failures ride on it. FIRST: 29 of those values are ones HeroUI would otherwise compute with color-mix(in oklab, ...) at runtime, and four of them CARRY TEXT — Alert tints its title with --color-success-soft-foreground. A colour the stylesheet computes is a colour the contrast gate never measured, so the generator computes them and emitHeroui REFUSES TO EMIT when a checked pairing fails. SECOND, and less obvious: uniwind normalises every CSS variable through culori.parse then formatHex ON DEVICE, and implements colorMix with culori.interpolate. So a non-hex value in this file hands the OKLCh-to-sRGB conversion that ADR-0043 makes ours to a third party, while the gate holds a number our own implementation derived — two implementations of one conversion, disagreeing in the fifth decimal, invisible until someone photographed two devices. THE GENERAL SHAPE: a generated artefact consumed by a dependency's runtime is only as authoritative as the notation it is written in; expressiveness in the file is authority handed away. THE GUARD IS REAL AND PROVEN: emitHeroui scans its own output and throws on any declaration carrying oklch(, color-mix(, rgb(, hsl(, lab( or lch(, and the pairing check has a decoy that drives status.ok onto the background and asserts the failure names --color-success-soft-foreground before asserting the throw. NOT COVERED: the values HeroUI reads that we do not override, and any future Uniwind feature that only accepts a colour function.

@irodora/ui is now built on heroui-native, which styles through className, and Uniwind resolves className in its METRO plugin. Jest never runs Metro. So a component that routes colour through a class renders in the a11y harness with NO COLOURS IN ITS TREE, and every colour check in the conformance suite iterates over an empty list — reporting nothing, printing as a pass, indistinguishable from a component whose every colour resolved. Measured, not feared: a real heroui-native Button came back with className, a transform, and backgroundColor: "invalid". THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the reusable part: build-time style resolution buys runtime performance by moving work to where the test runner is not, and the second half of that trade is never in the library's documentation. THE GUARDS ARE REAL AND PROVEN: lint rejects a colour utility class or an arbitrary colour value inside a className in packages/ui, with two decoys in verify-guards.mjs; the conformance suite fails a registered subject whose tree carries no resolved colour at all, with a fixture that is the exact HeroUI tree plus a control that passes; and verify-motion rejects a component that allows HeroUI's highlight or ripple, which animate backgroundColor inside a dependency the style scan cannot read. NOT COVERED: a component that paints SOME colours through style and routes others through a class — lint is the only defence there — and a class name assembled at runtime.

THIS LINK DID NOT MATTER UNTIL F-012, AND NOW EVERY PUBLISHED RECORD RESTS ON IT. Section 5 of licensing-and-provenance.md is a hand-edited markdown table, and parseRegister reads its COLUMN NAMES AND THEIR ORDER: renaming a heading, reordering one, or losing the "## 5. Source register" line stops the gate rather than letting it guess, and deleting or renaming a row fails every entry citing it. All 120 entries and all 5 palettes of 2026.08.1 cite the single row IRO-ED-001, so one careless edit to a document that reads like prose invalidates the entire corpus. IT BINDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND BOTH WERE WATCHED FAILING against the real corpus, not only the fixtures: an entry citing an unregistered id is rejected, and — the case that actually matters — an entry keeping the registered id while changing its `source` TEXT is rejected too, because that entry would display one provenance and be licensed under another. THE DOCUMENT STAYS PROSE ON PURPOSE. Generating this table from JSON would remove the brittleness and also remove the human review it exists for: it is a legal safeguard read by a person before each corpus version ships (ADR-0007). The brittleness is handled the only honest way — an unparseable table is a FAILURE, never an absence of constraint.

THE APP DOES NOT READ content/versions/; IT READS A COPY. ADR-0066 ships the pinned bundle as a generated TypeScript module carrying the bundle TEXT and the LEDGER’S root digest as two separate exports, because content/ sits outside apps/mobile and loadPublishedVersion takes text. So publishing a new corpus version without regenerating leaves the app on the OLD one, silently and with every other gate green: the old pair still verifies, because it is a valid bundle against its own valid ledger row. Nothing about the app would look wrong. THE GUARD IS `--check` INSIDE gate:content, and it was watched failing on a hand-edited count before being trusted. It compares the file on disk against what the CURRENT ledger’s last row produces, so a publish that forgets this step fails the build rather than shipping a stale corpus. THE SEPARATION OF TEXT AND DIGEST IS PART OF THE LINK, not a detail: a bundle carrying its own expected checksum verifies itself, so the generator reads the digest from index.json and never from the bundle, and a test asserts the bundle contains no self-describing root digest that a careless call site could pass instead.

A MIGRATION IS APPLIED ON A STRANGER’S PHONE AND CANNOT BE ROLLED BACK. There is no server to coordinate one, and `migrate.ts` has no `down` on purpose — correcting a bad migration means shipping the next one. So every dependent has to move in the same commit. The three that are not obvious: THE ARCHIVE reads `SELECT *`, so a new column silently joins the backup format and the canonical digest FR-58 compares byte for byte; THE CONFORMANCE SUITE is what makes a green CI run say anything about the device driver, so a table the suite does not exercise is a table proven on `node:sqlite` alone; and `SCHEMA_VERSION` gates an older build opening a newer database, which now REFUSES rather than guessing — correct, and reachable for the first time since F-020 raised it to 2. The guard is gate:test rather than typecheck because none of this is a type error: SQL is a string, and a column the repository forgot to write is a runtime null on a device. F-026 EXERCISED EVERY CLAUSE ABOVE AND ADDED ONE. Migration 3 brings two tables — `personal_color_profile` and `profile_dimension_color` — so `SYNC_TABLES` grew, and because `ARCHIVE_TABLES = [...SYNC_TABLES]` the backup format and its canonical digest took both WITHOUT ANYONE EDITING archive.ts. That is the link working by construction rather than by vigilance, and it is the reason the derivation of ARCHIVE_TABLES from SYNC_TABLES is worth more than a second list would be. Three conformance checks were added for the same reason F-020 added two: a profile is written across two tables and twenty-four columns, so its durability and its rollback are different claims from a single row’s. THE NEW CLAUSE IS NFR-22: `migrate()` now refuses a ladder that would add a prohibited column AND a database that already has one, so a migration is no longer only a thing that must be accompanied — it is a thing that can be REJECTED. `prohibited.ts` is therefore a dependent of this link in a direction the others are not: it reads MIGRATIONS as data, and a migration written without knowing it exists still cannot apply.

SINCE F-020 `parsePalette` HAS A SECOND CALLER, AND IT IS NOT A BUILD STEP. It runs on a device every time somebody saves a palette (FR-49, ADR-0067) — deliberately, because the two rules a palette EDITOR breaks are the two the schema already states: at least one anchor, and ranks contiguous from 1. What that buys in correctness it costs in reach: tightening the schema for editorial records — requiring `sourceUrl`, lengthening MIN_DERIVATION, adding a provenance field — now breaks SAVING ON A PHONE, with no compile error, because the device record is assembled as `unknown` and only the parse decides. The content gate would stay green throughout: `content/palettes/*.json` would be updated in the same commit and the app would not be. The guard is the round-trip in packages/store/test/palette.test.ts plus the malformed-draft table in apps/mobile/test/palette.test.ts, which fail on exactly that change.

THE CACHE KEY DECIDES WHETHER A GATE RAN, AND NOTHING ELSE REPORTS THAT IT DID NOT. `pnpm test` printed "31 successful, 31 total — 26 cached" while --force was red in four tests, for two independent reasons: a task is keyed on the inputs of the package it runs in, so eight design-tokens tests reading docs/design/design-system.manifest.json were cached over a change that fails seven of them; and the global hash contains `.nvmrc` as a GIT BLOB and `engines` as a RANGE, neither of which is the runtime executing — so a cache made on Node 24 is replayed on Node 22, where the bitwise fixtures differ by ULP. THIS IS CRITICAL BECAUSE IT IS UPSTREAM OF EVERY OTHER GUARD IN THIS GRAPH: E-001, E-003, E-007, E-013 and E-023 all name a gate as their guard, and a gate that replays a cached pass discharges none of them. A change to globalDependencies, globalEnv or the root scripts therefore changes what every other link is worth. THE GUARD IS verify-cache-scope.mjs, which enforces both halves — a test may not read past its package unless the target is a declared global dependency (an unresolvable path counts as unaccounted, failing closed), and a cached task must be started by scripts/gate.mjs, which is what puts the exact Node and package-manager versions into the key. Both were watched failing before being trusted: 6 planted cases through --prove with the baseline green either side, and rule 2 watched going red on a script reverted to a bare `turbo run test`. WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, printed on every run: a path assembled at run time or read through a helper it cannot follow.

THE LEXICON AND THE CORPUS TAXONOMY DEFINE THE SAME WORDS, and before F-021 only one of them existed. "dark" is now a numeric OKLCh region in content/rules AND an authored `taxonomy.lightnessBand` on every entry, which the Atlas filters on. Two definitions of one word drift, and the one that drifts is whichever nobody is looking at — so gate 11 asserts every authored band falls inside the lexicon region of the same name, 175 agreements over 28 terms, printed on every run so a green check over ZERO entries cannot read as coverage. IT HAS ALREADY PAID: the boundaries were first written as round numbers and the check found that 0.40 sits a MILLIONTH above the lowest entry filed as mid (do-ma at 0.3999990449505662), which would have excluded it from every query for a medium colour, silently and forever. THE LINK RUNS BOTH WAYS, which is what makes it worth recording: editing a BOUNDARY breaks entries nobody touched, and adding an ENTRY across a boundary breaks a lexicon nobody touched. THE THIRD DESTINATION IS THE FONT. The lexicon’s Japanese terms are typed INTO the Finder and echoed in the field, so they render in the app’s own subset exactly as a colour name does — verify-font-coverage.mjs now reads them, and doing so immediately found two codepoints (淡, 鮮) that nothing else required. THE FOURTH is the generated module: publishing a lexicon without regenerating leaves the app on the old vocabulary with every other gate green, which is E-022’s shape, guarded the same way by generate-rules-bundle.mjs --check inside gate 11. PUBLISHING A LEXICON ALSO REACHES GATE 15, which nobody had noticed until F-096. `generate-rules-bundle.mjs` emits the ledger checksum into apps/mobile/src/rules/generated/lexicon.ts as LEXICON_DIGEST, and a 64-hex literal in shipped source is the shape of a SQLCipher key — so `verify-no-key-material.mjs` reported a published digest as a possible key and gate 15 went RED, from F-021 (f0f1f6c) onward. It stayed invisible for four features because the workstation had no gitleaks and reported gate 15 as "partly run", and because CI stopped at the install step before ever reaching it (F-098). THE FIX WAS NOT TO EXEMPT THE PATH: a key written into a generated file is exactly as dangerous as one written by hand. The discriminator is the LEDGER, so the ledger is now every place this repository publishes a checksum — content/versions/ and content/rules/index.json — and each source is probed on every run with a digest it actually carries, because the old single probe used a hard-coded test vector that is silent whether or not either ledger file was read. PUBLISHING A THIRD KIND OF VERSIONED CONTENT MEANS ADDING ITS LEDGER TO LEDGER_SOURCES. Forgetting turns gate 15 red on something correct, which is the failure that gets a security gate ignored rather than the one that gets it fixed.

E-007 ALREADY SAYS A TOKEN CHANGE IS A CONTRAST CHANGE IN BOTH THEMES, AND IT STOPPED AT COMPONENTS. Since F-023 the tokens also travel OUT of the app: cardSvg bakes background, foreground, foreground.2 and BOTH swatch.hairline tones into an SVG document as literal values, because an SVG has no other way to carry a colour. That is E-019 shape — a generated artefact a dependency evaluates later — with one difference that matters: a stylesheet is regenerated on every build and a shared card is not. A card somebody sent last week keeps the token values it was built with, and no gate reaches it. WHAT IS GUARDED: every colour in a freshly built document must be a design-token value or the entry own published hex, over all 120 entries in BOTH themes, with a decoy proving a planted colour is reported. WHAT IS NOT: the keyline tones are inherited from F-068 rather than re-derived here, so a manifest change that moved swatch.hairline without re-running swatch-edge.test.ts would keep this link green while the card lost its edge against a near-white sample. That is why the card reuses the TOKENS instead of drawing a border, and why the two checks are complementary rather than redundant.

THE KEY SET COMES FROM CORPUS DATA, SO THE COMPILER CANNOT CHECK IT. Every other user-facing string in this app is a key in an enumerated TypeScript record whose completeness `tsc` proves (ADR-0056). A family is different: `taxonomy.family` is authored in content/colors, so the set of words that must exist is decided by a PUBLISH rather than by source — and tsc cannot see a key set that comes from JSON. That is why F-018 left the Atlas rendering `blue-grey` and `off-white` in the ja locale rather than adding a lookup table: a table in the app would be enumerated against a set the corpus controls, and a family added by a future publish would render blank or fall back to English, which ADR-0028 forbids precisely because fallback makes a gap invisible. SO COMPLETENESS MOVED FROM THE COMPILER TO GATE 11, and the link runs BOTH ways: publishing an entry with a new family breaks the vocabulary, and removing a vocabulary row breaks the corpus. A row nobody uses fails too — a dead row is how a live gap gets waved through later, the same rule the source register and the advisory register both carry. THE THIRD DESTINATION IS THE FONT, and it caught something: the Japanese family words render on the Atlas filter, every Atlas row and the detail screen, so verify-font-coverage.mjs now reads them — and doing so immediately reported 鼠 and 陶, which nothing else in the repository required. 鼠 alone appears in six of the 25 families, so a Japanese reader would have seen tofu on most of the grey filter chips. THE LOOKUP IS TOTAL OR IT THROWS: familyLabel has no fallback to the slug, because returning `blue-grey` quietly is the behaviour that let this survive from F-018 to F-090 in the first place.

EMITTING A VALUE IS NOT APPLYING A DECISION. Every value in packages/design-tokens/src/generated/ is byte-compared against the manifest by emit.test.ts and again by generate-design-tokens.mjs --check, so we know each one is CORRECT. Nothing asked whether it was USED — and F-019 found nativeNumericFeature that way by hand, emitted and exported and reaching no component, for as long as nobody happened to look. ADR-0054 had already settled the identical question for COMPONENTS; verify-token-reach.mjs is the same closure over VALUES, in gate 8 beside a11y-scope.mjs. THREE RULES DECIDE WHETHER IT IS WORTH ANYTHING. packages/ui/src/testing/ is NOT a reader, because a token read only by the conformance checker exists so a CHECK can enforce it and is not a painted pixel — without that exclusion, four findings would have been absorbed silently. Reach propagates through OBJECT VALUES (Surface resolves surface.1 through nativeElevation, and that name appears nowhere as a literal) but never through KEYS (theme.tsx reads nativeColors, whose keys are all 33 colour tokens) and never through ARRAY ELEMENTS (a membership test is a question nobody answers with the token). An object is looked up; a list is looked in. COMMENTS ARE NOT CODE, and the proof found that, not a reading: border.strong was removed from all five components that use it and the check still called it reached, because Button.tsx mentions it in backticks in a comment. Every JSDoc example in a repository that comments this heavily was counting as a consumer. Stripping comments turned three more tokens honest, including foreground.3 — the token whose entire purpose is to be restricted — whose every mention in the reader zone is prose about why it is dangerous. THE ESCAPE HATCH RUNS BOTH WAYS: .harness/verification/unreached-tokens.json declares 34 names with a why and a citation, prints the whole list on every run rather than only on a failure, and FAILS on a declaration for a token that IS read. One of its entries is a defect rather than an exemption — nativeSpacing is imported by nothing while 69 hand-written values contradict the scale, filed as F-095 and cited from the declaration.

links.guard: gate:test (apps/mobile/test/profile.test.ts — every trial checked against the published OKLCh)
links.rationale: TWELVE CONSTANTS NAME CORPUS SLUGS AND ENCODE A CLAIM ABOUT THE VALUES BEHIND THEM: that each comparison separates on its own axis and stays matched on the others. Nothing in the type system holds that. A temperature trial is two entries matched in OKLCh L and C and opposed in hue class — move one entry 0.05 in L at the next publish and the same question is now partly about lightness, the answer still tallies, the profile still looks reasonable, and NOTHING ON THE SCREEN LOOKS DIFFERENT. This is E-022’s shape aimed at a different destination: E-022 asks whether the bundle the app reads is the one that was published; this asks whether a constant DESCRIBING the bundle’s contents still means what it said. The guard reads the published values rather than the authored ones and names the trial that fails, with a decoy asserting the separation thresholds can reject a pair — without it "every trial clears the bound" would also be true of a bound of zero. It is severity high rather than medium because the failure is silent by construction and the output is a personal profile that F-028 will weight recommendations by. F-027 ADDED A SECOND CONSUMER THAT DOES NOT NAME A SLUG. `photo.ts` calls the same three list derivations over the same published entries, so a corpus publish moves a photo estimate’s neutrals, accents and avoid list exactly as it moves a guided one — and unlike the trials, nothing about that dependency is visible as a constant somebody could read. It is caught because the two paths SHARE the derivations rather than agreeing today: the guided tests assert those lists exactly, so a change reaching one path fails there.

links.guard: gate:test (apps/mobile/test/profile.test.ts — the reading’s cap is asserted to reach the estimate, with a baseline)
links.rationale: A LENS READING’S CONFIDENCE WAS A NUMBER SHOWN BESIDE A COLOUR. It is now the ceiling on seven profile dimensions, and F-028 will weight recommendations by those. So a change to ANY of the three inputs `cappedConfidence` combines — SPACE_CONFIDENCE_CEILING, the illumination assessment, the quality assessment — silently changes how much authority a personal profile carries, one subsystem away from where it was edited. THE TYPE CANNOT SEE IT: the field stays a number in [0,1] and every signature is unchanged, so typecheck is green through the whole thing. The guard is a test that asserts a poor reading produces a less confident estimate AND that a good one produces the ceiling — the baseline half matters, because "the cap is applied" is indistinguishable from "the value is constant" without it. What the guard does NOT cover is whether the ceilings are the right numbers; they are conventions (NFR-2) and F-063 is what would replace them with measurements.

EVERY WORKSPACE MANIFEST IS AN INPUT TO ONE SHARED ARTEFACT, and every gate is downstream of it. pnpm-workspace.yaml names the projects and carries the overrides; each package.json declares dependencies; pnpm-lock.yaml resolves all of them at once; and CI installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which refuses unless the lockfile resolves exactly what the manifests declare — three dependency sections, compared VERBATIM, plus overrides. Install is step nine of the CI job and the seventeen steps after it do not run when it fails, so a three-line omission in a generated file reads as a total build outage. IT HAPPENED: F-020 (9ce0926) added `@irodora/corpus: workspace:*` to packages/store and nothing regenerated the lockfile, and three pushes were red on an install step nobody had touched. THE REASON IT IS CRITICAL RATHER THAN HIGH is that it broke while every local signal said it was fine: pnpm could not run on the workstation at all (Node 22 and pnpm 9 against engines demanding 24 and 11), a hand-made junction stood in for the workspace link, and imports, typecheck and tests all passed against it. A dependency edge that lives in three places — the manifest, the lockfile, node_modules — can be true in two of them and false where it counts, with no compiler error and no failing test. GUARDED IN GATE 0 rather than at install, because gate 0 runs before install, on Node built-ins, on a clean clone, and is therefore the only check that can report a stale lockfile to somebody who cannot run pnpm. Projects come from the globs rather than a hard-coded list, and a glob the parser cannot expand FAILS rather than being skipped. PROVEN by verify-lockfile-proof.mjs: seven cases, five red and two green, the second control being a project that declares nothing — `tests/bench: {}` is that shape, and reading it as absent would have failed a correct lockfile on day one.

THE WARM/COOL RULE NOW EXISTS TWICE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS CANONICAL. `hueBias` in the engine and `biasFromHue` in `apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts` compute the same thing — how warm a hue is, as a signed distance between two reference poles — and they were written two features apart with the same constants (60 and 240) by the same reasoning. THIS IS THE E-008 SHAPE, and E-008 states the consequence exactly: a second implementation makes the same input measure differently on two surfaces, and NO SINGLE-PLATFORM TEST CAN SEE IT. Both sides pass their own tests today. GUARD: NONE, HONESTLY. The fix is for the app to import the engine, and it cannot: `apps/mobile/node_modules/@irodora/` has no `recommendation` link and `pnpm install` refuses on this workstation (Node 22.16.0 against engines demanding 24.19.0). A cross-package agreement test was considered and rejected — the app file imports the corpus bundle, so a package test importing it would drag app dependencies across a layering boundary to check two numbers, and a check whose model is wrong is worse than an absent one. Scraping the constants out of the source would compare two literals while the ALGORITHMS drifted, which is the half that actually matters. WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO CARRY: the poles are a RULE SET field in the engine, so the engine’s copy is already content-versioned and the app’s is not — the drift, when it comes, will be the app holding a constant the content moved past. F-099 deletes the duplicate the day the app can depend on the package, and this link is what will still be here to say so.
